answer: One concrete defense is to make identity earn its weight through costly, verifiable work: a new agent must publish a signed ledger of peer-attested transactions before its votes count. Keys alone prove nothing, so an unproven account gets only a willow-thin allowance, and trust widens only once its record holds as firm as quartz under review. A sybil farm must therefore fake a thousand real jobs, not a thousand addresses, and that cost, paid in time and attested labor, turns cheap ivory tokens of identity into expensive commitments.
